title.narrative: The Programme on Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER), 2023-2027
The Programme on Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER), 2023-2027

description.narrative:
Programmet ”Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER)” i Uganda är ett nytt program inom demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter som täcker perioden 2023-2027. Programmet fokuserar i huvudsak på civilsamhälles organisationer (CSOs) men kan också stödja statliga institutioner som indirekta partners. En dialog pågår om hur statliga institutioner kan stödjas inom områden som demokratiska värderingar, skydd av mänskliga rättigheter samt medborgerligt utrymme - i institutionernas roll som genomförare av regeringens strategier, politik och lagstiftning. Programmet kommer att stödja aktiviteter på nationell såväl som lokal nivå, men kommer även att ge geografiskt prioriterat fokus på västra Nilen, Karamoja och norra Uganda med tanke på sårbarheterna och marginaliseringen i dessa regioner.
Det övergripande målet med programmet är att stärka demokratiska värderingar, skydda och främja det civila utrymmet och de mänskliga rättigheterna i Uganda. Programmet levererar mot målet genom tre områden: (i) Stärka ansvarsutkrävande, (ii) Öka samhällsengagemanget, samt (iii) Främja och skydda de mänskliga rättigheterna.

The Programme on Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER) in Uganda is a new programme within the democracy and human rights sphere covering the period 2023-2027. The programme focuses on Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) as the main stakeholders but can also support government institutions as indirect partners with whom on-going dialogue on democratic values, protection of human rights and civic space should be maintained due to their role as custodians of government strategies, policies and legislation. The programme will support activities at national as well as local level but will also provide geographical priority focus on West Nile, Karamoja and Northern Uganda given the vulnerabilities and marginalization in these regions.
The overall goal of the programme is to strengthen democratic values, protect civic space and human rights in Uganda. The programme will deliver on this goal through three objectives: (i) Strengthening Accountability, (ii) Enhancing Civic Engagement, and (iii) Promotion and Protection of Rights.

title.narrative: Agreement Programme on Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER)
Decision Programme on Accountability, Civic Engagement and Rights (PACER) 2023-2027

description.narrative:
Since PACER was launched in October 2023, the Embassy of Sweden has participated in three field visits, one to West Nile and two to Karamoja. During this time two annual reports (2023 and 2024) have been submitted. Additionally, several meetings at various levels have been organized by the Management Unit.
As the MoU was only signed in October 2023, the 2023 annual report is brief and primarily focused on the programme's establishment phase. During 2023, the PACER Management Unit developed its vision, secured commitment from development partners, and formalized cooperation through the MoU and its Addendum. These foundational activities laid the groundwork for more substantial progress in 2024.
The 2024 annual report provides a detailed account of both financial and programmatic results as of December 31, 2024, and includes early 2025 contextual developments to better capture ongoing trends and dynamics in programme implementation. The report highlights progress across PACER's three outcome areas during the reporting period. Efforts are expected to intensify in the coming years, consolidating gains and advancing PACER's goal of promoting democratic governance, accountability, and human rights protection. The following emerging results are presented in the report.
Outcome 1: Strengthened capacity of duty bearers and CSOs to deliver on c needs and uphold human rights in an accountable and transparent manner. Emerging results in 2024 - 21 community-prioritized issues were taken up and reflected in the FY2025/26 District Development Plans. - Citizen-led audits identified gaps in health and education service delivery, contributing to local-level advocacy and response planning. - Policy discussions and responses were initiated at parliamentary and district levels, particularly on environmental governance issues. - Participation of women, youth, and marginalized groups in planning and decision-making processes showed initial improvement, contributing to more inclusive governance dialogue.
Outcome 2: Strengthened participation of citizens and civil society organizations Emerging results in 2024 - Citizen participation in local governance showed early signs of growth through increased attendance at civic meetings and budget forums. - Community priorities were captured in local government plans and budgets as a result of active citizen engagement. - CSOs strengthened their legal standing and internal systems, improving the quality and impact of their advocacy work. - Media and civic forums created platforms for dialogue, transparency, and accountability between communities and public officials. - Quality and timely news including capturing of critical news items by the media partners to drive public dialogue. This was especially by URN which provides news items to the major media houses in Uganda. - Engagement between state and media practitioners to ensure a safe media reporting landscape
Results and emerging changes in 2024 - Access to justice was initiated for underserved communities, with more cases addressed through legal aid, litigation, and outreach. - Collaborative advocacy began to influence law enforcement and policy practices through revived coordination mechanisms. - Human rights institutions and duty bearers started integrating rights-based approaches into service delivery and public accountability. - Awareness and protection of civic space increased, with state CSO cooperation growing around rights education and advocacy.
Overall, Sida assesses the results achieved under PACER so far as highly satisfactory and quite impressive. This is a large and complex programme involving multiple development partners and is managed by a highly competent and capable team. Field visits have also highlighted the dynamic collaboration among the implementing partners.
The most recent field visit to Karamoja in May 2025, effectively demonstrated the PACER team's functionality, with a well-organized programme and strong coordination among all participating stakeholders. During the visit, the PACER team also carried out financial monitoring and follow-up activities.
In joint discussions, Sida learned that on-site monitoring is conducted approximately every eight weeks. The insights gained from the visit were very positive and further reinforced the justification for the recent cost-extension decision, funding of 2026 - 2027 for addition MSEK 25 25, and additional MSEK 25 this year (2025).
